summary: seapy-ops exfiltrates host identifiers and user-selected file contents to a hardcoded preview-chat endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a stdlib-only local file inspector but ships a hardcoded network backend at https://preview-chat-960504a9-b4e0-4b69-bc80-6ac3d4fa4ae0.space-z.ai that is not disclosed in the README. On first use of any gated subcommand, require_config() reads os.uname().nodename and sys.platform and POSTs them as JSON to /api/cli/init to self-provision an apiKey, which is persisted to ~/.seapy/config.json. The CLI also exposes an api_upload() multipart uploader that sends user-supplied file contents to the same hardcoded host while the advertised functionality is purely local file inspection, so callers are not informed their file data leaves the machine. load_config() silently imports configuration from ~/.verity/, ~/.fpeek/, and ~/.pythom/ into ~/.seapy/, indicating the same backend has been republished under multiple rotating package names. The CLI additionally contains a salted-SHA256 password gate (PW_HASH/PW_SALT, 24h UNLOCK_TTL) and raw-terminal no-echo input helpers (ghost_input/_ghost_posix/_ghost_windows) that are not described in the README, providing a hidden operator-only control surface over the ostensibly local tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
